open_questions: Centroid is inconclusive (no sector with clear difference image) so off-target blend at >3 px cannot be fully excluded; follow-up photometry with a different aperture/detector would test for blend.
dossier.public_summary: The dip is flat and planet-sized at 2.39 Earth radii with no odd-even difference or secondary, but the six individual transits have wildly different depths driven by two strong outliers and starspot signals of thousands of ppm. The long duration and density mismatch versus the M dwarf, combined with variability at a rotation harmonic, make spots/systematics landing in the transit window a better explanation than a planet. The sky location cannot yet be confirmed and photometric follow-up is still needed to rule out a blend.

reasons.why: Individual transit depths are completely inconsistent (chi2 84.6 dof5), not expected for a stable planet; top 3 carry 0.801 of signal with outliers at 4183 ppm (+5.6 sigma) and -167 ppm (-5.5 sigma). This points to a few bad/deleterious events driving the detection.
Signal is dominated by a small subset of transits, consistent with stellar variability / systematics landing in the transit window rather than a periodic planet.

Observed duration 3.999 h vs central 2.738 h is long for a central transit; fit density ratio -1.64 and star_density_penalty 42.69 indicate shape is inconsistent with the TIC M dwarf (R=0.519) despite b=0.9049 high impact parameter allowing a long duration.

High-variability spotted M dwarf; large spot amplitudes and rotation signals coinciding with the 12.7 d period provide an alternative explanation for variable-depth dips, supporting that the signal is noise/variability.
reasons.value: sector 55 amplitude 2055 ppm, sector 81 2742 ppm, sector 82 5701 ppm with signal_over_rotation 3.426

reasons.why: Flat bottom argues against a V-shaped grazing binary, but flat bottom alone does not make a planet — with no centroid (centroid.verdict inconclusive) and no Gaia nighbour within 1 px able to cause it, the variability-driven depth changes and duration mismatch favour a false positive.
